propositions.text: The claimant is 26 years old, a Mexican citizen, claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97 of IRPA.
propositions.quote: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, the claimant, 26 years old, a citizen of Mexico, is basing his refugee protection claim on sections 96-membership in the particular social group of homosexuals-and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

propositions.text: The claimant alleges facts supporting his refugee claim under sections 96 and 97 of IRPA.
propositions.quote: In support of his claim, he is alleging the following facts.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a 26-year-old Mexican citizen, claims refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97, alleging supporting facts.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges he is homosexual and his problems with his lover began in 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that he is homosexual and that his problems with his lover began in XXXX 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he is homosexual and had problems with his lover starting in 2008.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges he was in a romantic relationship with XXXX since 2006.
propositions.quote: He had been in a romantic relationship with XXXX since XXX 2006.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges a romantic relationship with XXXX since 2006.

propositions.text: In March 2008, the claimant met a prominent politician XXXX who became his secret lover due to social standing.
propositions.quote: In March 2008, he met a prominent politician, XXXX, at the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. XXXXX displayed an interest in the claimant by giving him expensive presents and asking him out several times. A month later, they became lovers and started having a secret affair because of XXXXX high social standing in the community.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he met and secretly dated a prominent politician XXXX starting March 2008.

propositions.text: The claimant ended the relationship with XXXX who then harassed him and threatened to get rid of XXXX.
propositions.quote: The claimant ended this relationship with XXXXX because he was not proud of deceiving XXXXX. XXXX was offended and started harassing the claimant. One day, he told the claimant that he was going to get rid of XXXX because he could not let go of his relationship with the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant ended the relationship; XXXX harassed and threatened him to get rid of XXXX.

propositions.text: The claimant began noticing strange people near where he and XXXX lived.
propositions.quote: At this time, the claimant began noticing strange people where he and XXXX lived.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant noticed strange people near his residence with XXXX.

propositions.text: The claimant warned XXXX he would reveal evidence of their relationship if harassment continued.
propositions.quote: Tired of the threats, the claimant warned XXXXX that if he did not leave him alone, he would reveal the cards, gifts and photographs that XXXXX had given him-undeniable evidence of the relationship that would damage XXXXX image in the community.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant warned XXXX he would expose evidence of their relationship if harassment persisted.

propositions.text: The police informed the claimant that XXXX was killed; claimant identified the body but did not report threats due to police mockery.
propositions.quote: A few days later, the police called the claimant to tell him that XXXX had been killed. The claimant went to the police station to identify the body. The claimant wanted to report XXXXX threats to the police, but he changed his mind when they made fun of him after he told them that XXXX was his lover.

paragraphs.summary: Police told claimant XXXX was killed; he identified the body but did not report threats due to police mockery.

propositions.text: The claimant fled to a friend's home; XXXX called to warn he knew claimant's location.
propositions.quote: The claimant went to live with a friend. The next day, XXXXX called the claimant on his cellphone to warn him that he knew where he was.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant hid with a friend but XXXX warned he knew his location.

propositions.text: The claimant sought refuge in another city; XXXX called again threatening to kill him if he refused to return.
propositions.quote: The claimant went to seek refuge in the city of XXXXX. However, two days later, XXXXX called him again. He said that it was his last chance to go back to him; if he refused, he would kill him that same day.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fled to another city; XXXX threatened to kill him if he did not return.

propositions.text: The claimant changed his phone number and traveled to XXXXXXXX; XXXX called again threatening to kill him within 24 hours.
propositions.quote: The claimant immediately his changed telephone number and travelled to XXXXXXXX. However, six days later, XXXXX called him on his cellphone again and warned him that he was going to kill him within 24 hours.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant changed phone number and location; XXXX threatened to kill him within 24 hours.

propositions.text: The claimant left Mexico fearing for his life and claimed refugee protection in Montréal on June 27, 2008.
propositions.quote:
Fearing for his life, the claimant left his country on XXXXX, 2008.

He claimed refugee protection in Montréal on June 27, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fled Mexico fearing for his life and claimed refugee protection in Montréal on June 27, 2008.

propositions.text: The panel determines the refugee claim cannot be allowed for stated reasons.
propositions.quote: After hearing the claimant's testimony and analyzing all of the evidence, the panel determines that this claim cannot be allowed, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The panel decides the refugee claim is not allowed for reasons to follow.

propositions.text: The claimant's marriage in Montréal in 2010 establishes nexus with the social group of homosexuals under section 96.
propositions.quote: Based on the claimant's testimony, according to which he married XXXXX on XXXXXX, 2010, in Montréal, the panel concludes that there is a nexus with one of the five grounds in section 96, that is, membership in the particular social group of homosexuals.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's marriage establishes nexus with the social group of homosexuals under section 96.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity was established satisfactorily with Mexican passport and CIC copies on file.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction. He appeared before the authorities at the port of entry with his Mexican passport, which was seized by Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC), and copies of which are on file.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's identity established satisfactorily by passport and CIC records.

propositions.text: The claimant's testimony was not credible, with examples to follow.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony was not credible. The following are some examples.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's testimony not credible, citing examples.

propositions.text: The claimant fears XXXX will kill him if he returns to Mexico.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he still fears XXXXX because he is convinced that this individual will kill him as soon as he returns to Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fears XXXX will kill him upon return to Mexico.

propositions.text: The claimant testified XXXX is a well-known politician in XXXXX and belongs to the 'XXX' party, which he described.
propositions.quote: When asked about XXXXX profile, the claimant testified that he is a well-known politician in XXXXX. When asked what political party XXXXX belongs to, the claimant answered the "XXX"; when asked what this acronym stood for, the claimant stated that it stood for the XXXXXXXXXXX XXXXX and that XXXXX had XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified XXXX is a well-known politician belonging to the 'XXX' party, describing the acronym and history.

propositions.text: The panel could not find a party called 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' in the evidence; the party 'XXX' is the second-largest in Mexico's chamber of deputies.
propositions.quote: Despite the extensive amount of evidence submitted as A-1, the panel could not find a party called the [translation] "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX." The documentary evidence indicates that the Party XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, abbreviated XXX, is the second-largest parliamentary group in Mexico's chamber of deputies.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no party called 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'; 'XXX' is the second-largest party in Mexico's chamber of deputies.

propositions.text: No evidence supports the existence of politician XXXX or his political role in 2008; this undermines claimant's story.
propositions.quote: In addition, there is no information on a politician named XXXXXXXXXX in the extensive evidence entered on the record. Furthermore, there is no evidence to corroborate the claimant's statements that XXXXX was XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX in 2008. Consequently, the panel is of the opinion, based on the fact that XXXXX is not mentioned in the documentary evidence submitted and on a balance of probabilities, that XXXXX is not currently part of the political scene in Mexico. This leads the panel to question the truthfulness of the claimant's entire story. The following analysis supports this conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no evidence of politician XXXX or his role, leading to doubts about the claimant's story.

propositions.text: Claimant testified affair with XXXXX began and ended on specific dates in 2008, and XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that his affair with this individual began on XXXXX, 2008, and that he ended the relationship by telephone on XXXXX, 2008. When asked whether XXXXX had ever been to his home, he answered that XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified that his affair with XXXXX began and ended on specific 2008 dates and that XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door.

propositions.text: Claimant testified next face-to-face meeting with XXXXX was on a specific 2008 date at his workplace, where XXXXX mentioned getting rid of XXXXX.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that his next face-to-face meeting with XXXXX was on XXXXX, 2008, at the XXXXXXXXXXXXXX, where the claimant worked. He also testified that it was on this date that XXXXX had mentioned that he was going to get rid of XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified his next meeting with XXXXX was on a 2008 date at work, where XXXXX said he would get rid of XXXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant testified noticing strange people in a pickup truck outside his home on a 2008 date, identified as XXXXX security staff who accompanied them to meetings.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that it was on XXXXX, 2008, that he had noticed strange people in a pickup truck outside his home. He added that these were XXXXX employees. When asked to explain how he knew that, the claimant added that these people were members of XXXXX security staff. Questioned further, he added that these six security officers usually accompanied them to the various locations where the claimant and XXXXX met.

propositions.text: Panel asked claimant why he stated he had 'started noticing strange people' rather than that it was strange they were in his neighbourhood.
propositions.quote: In light of this testimony, the claimant was asked to explain why, in paragraph 10 of his narrative, he stated that he had [translation] "started noticing strange people" where he lived.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about strange people outside his home identified as XXXXX security staff; the panel questioned his wording about noticing them.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's narrative clearly alleged strangers outside his house, not that it was strange they were in his neighbourhood.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant clearly alleged in his narrative that the people outside his house were strange people or strangers, not [translation] "that it was strange that these people were in his neighbourhood."

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's explanation for inconsistency flagrant and undermines his credibility.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant tried to brush aside the inconsistency, which the panel found to be flagrant. It is reasonable to expect the claimant to specifically and clearly disclose that he had recognized XXXXX security officers in his neighbourhood, if that was the case. The panel concludes that the inconsistency between his testimony and the information in his narrative undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's explanation for inconsistency flagrant and undermines his credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant initially testified telephone contact with XXXXX on a date, then amended to no contact between those dates.
propositions.quote: When asked whether he had had any contact with XXXXX between XXXX and XX, 2008, the claimant initially testified that they had talked on the telephone on XXXX; he then amended his testimony and stated that there had not been any contact between these dates.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant initially testified to telephone contact with XXXXX, then amended to no contact between those dates.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he threatened to reveal cards, gifts, photos from XXXXX after XXXXX was killed, contradicting narrative stating threat before murder.
propositions.quote: Given this testimony, the panel asked the claimant about the date on which he allegedly threatened to reveal the cards, gifts and photographs from XXXXX. He answered, [translation] "After XXXXX was killed." In light of this testimony, the claimant was asked to explain why, in paragraph 11 of his narrative, he stated he had threatened XXXXX before XXXXX murder.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation of confusing events and threatening on a different date does not satisfy the panel.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he was stressed and nervous, that he had confused the events and that he had threatened XXXXX on XXXX. This explanation does not satisfy the panel, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's explanation for contradicting threat dates does not satisfy the panel.

propositions.text: It is reasonable to expect claimant to speak about alleged experiences with consistency, integrity and accuracy.
propositions.quote: It is reasonable to expect the claimant to speak about his alleged experiences with consistency, integrity and accuracy, since, according to his testimony, these events are the reason he does not want to return to his country.

paragraphs.summary: The panel states it is reasonable to expect the claimant to speak about his experiences consistently and accurately.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he sought refuge with a friend, received threatening calls from XXXXX ordering him to return and give photographs or be killed.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he sought refuge with a friend on XXXXX. He added that on XXXXX, XXXXX called him on his cellphone to warn him to return and that this was when he decided to flee from XXXXX and go to a friend's home in XXXXX. The claimant stated that he stayed in XXXXX for two or three days, and that on XXXXX, 2008, XXXXX called and warned him that he knew where he was and ordered him to return to XXXXX. And although the claimant changed his telephone number, XXXXX managed to call him on XXXXX, while he was still in XXXXXXX, because he wanted the claimant to give him the photographs and gifts that he had given him within 24 hours or else he would kill him.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about seeking refuge and receiving threatening calls from XXXXX demanding photographs or threatening death.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he told XXXXX he had photographs but had deleted them; no mention of photos in narrative paragraph 15.
propositions.quote: The claimant subsequently testified that he had told XXXXX that he had the photographs; however, he had already deleted the photographs from his camera. When asked why there is no mention of any photographs in paragraph 15 of his narrative, the claimant answered, [translation] "I do not know."

propositions.text: Panel does not accept claimant's explanation for omission of photographs in narrative.
propositions.quote: This explanation does not satisfy the panel, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The panel does not accept the claimant's explanation for omitting photographs in his narrative.

propositions.text: Claimant alleged XXXXX wanted to resume romantic relationship and killed XXXXX for that reason alone.
propositions.quote: Throughout both his narrative and his testimony, the claimant alleged that XXXXX adamantly wanted to resume his romantic relationship with him. In the claimant's written allegations, XXXXX killed XXXXX for this reason alone.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleged XXXXX wanted to resume their relationship and killed XXXXX for that reason alone.

propositions.text: In narrative paragraph 15, claimant stated XXXXX threatened to kill him in 24 hours; later said XXXXX wanted incriminating photographs.
propositions.quote: However, in paragraph 15 of his narrative, the claimant stated that XXXXX last threats were "he told me he was going to kill me in 24 hours". When asked about this new element of his story, the claimant suddenly stated that what XXXXXX wanted was the incriminating [translation] "photographs."

propositions.text: Panel concludes claimant added new element to embellish claim and is not credible.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that the claimant added a new element to his story to embellish his refugee protection claim. The claimant is not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant added a new element about photographs to embellish his claim and is not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant testified XXXXX was killed by gunshot; newspaper reported murder as attempted theft; claimant did not submit article as name not mentioned and he did not keep it.
propositions.quote: When asked how XXXXX was killed, the claimant answered, [translation] "by gunshot." When asked whether the murder had been reported in the Mexican newspapers, the claimant testified that one newspaper report had described his murder as an attempted theft. When asked to explain why he had not submitted the newspaper article into evidence, the claimant testified that XXXXX name was not mentioned in the article and that he had not kept the article in question.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about XXXXX's gunshot death and a newspaper report describing it as attempted theft, but did not submit the article.

propositions.text: Claimant submitted faxed email from 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' dated 2011 to corroborate XXXXX murder.
propositions.quote: To corroborate XXXXX murder, at the outset of the hearing, the claimant submitted a faxed copy of an email from "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX," dated XXXXX, 2011.

propositions.text: Panel attaches little probative value to this document for reasons explained later.
propositions.quote: The panel attaches little probative value to this document, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant submitted a faxed email to corroborate XXXXX's murder, but the panel attaches little probative value to it.

propositions.text: Refugee Protection Division Rules require documents in other languages to have English or French translation and translator's declaration.
propositions.quote: First, subrule 28(1) of the Refugee Protection Division Rules states the following: All documents used at a proceeding must be in English or French or, if in another language, be provided with an English or French translation and a translator's declaration.

paragraphs.summary: The panel cites rule requiring translations and translator's declaration for documents in other languages.

propositions.text: No translator's declaration was provided for the document as required by rule 28.
propositions.quote: No translator's declaration was provided in accordance with the requirements of rule 28.

paragraphs.summary: No translator's declaration was provided for the document as required by rule 28.

propositions.text: Claimant testified person named XXXXXX was a lawyer and friend of a friend; document lacks header, address, or signature page usual for law firms.
propositions.quote: Second, when asked who this person named XXXXXX was, the claimant testified that he was a lawyer, [translation] "a friend of a friend." The document does not contain a header, an address or even a personalized signature page, which is a relatively common practice for law firms and which would have indicated to the panel that this was indeed a legal, probative and relevant document.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified the document's author was a lawyer friend of a friend, but the document lacks usual law firm features.

propositions.text: Panel finds no evidence in document establishing XXXXX was murdered as claimant described despite references to deceased boyfriend and estate.
propositions.quote: Finally, although the content mentions the [translation] "deceased boyfriend, XXXXX..." and [translation] "the deceased's estate in Family Court...," the panel is of the opinion that there is no evidence in this document establishing that XXXXX was murdered as the claimant described.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no evidence in the document establishing XXXXX was murdered as described by the claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant submitted another faxed email from a friend in Mexico dated 2011 at hearing outset.
propositions.quote: The claimant also submitted into evidence, at the outset of the hearing, another fax of a copy of an email from "XXXXXXXXXXXXXX," dated XXXXXX, 2011. When asked about this person's identity, the claimant testified that he was one of his friends in Mexico.

propositions.text: Panel attaches little probative value to this document for reasons explained later.
propositions.quote: The panel attaches little probative value to this document, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant submitted another faxed email from a friend in Mexico, but the panel attaches little probative value to it.

propositions.text: No translator's declaration was provided for this document as required by rule 28.
propositions.quote: Once again, no translator's declaration was provided in accordance with the requirements of rule 28.

propositions.text: Content is subjective, not from independent reliable source, produced to embellish claim.
propositions.quote: Second, the content of this document, produced only one week before the hearing, is highly subjective and does not come from an independent and reliable source. Based on the inconsistencies in this file, the panel concludes that this document was produced solely for the purpose of embellishing the refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no translator's declaration and that the document is subjective and produced to embellish the claim.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he had not travelled outside Mexico before Canada trip in 2008; passport issued five weeks before Canada trip.
propositions.quote: Finally, the claimant was asked whether he had travelled outside Mexico before he travelled to Canada in XXX 2008. He testified that he had not. Consequently, he was asked why his passport was issued to him on XXXXXX, 2008, five weeks before he left for Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant testified planned to travel to Cuba with XXXXX in July 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he had planned to travel with XXXXX to Cuba for a vacation at the end of July 2008.

propositions.text: Panel concludes claimant intended to travel to Canada in 2008 and invented persecution story to submit refugee claim after arrival.
propositions.quote: Based on the inconsistencies in this file and on a balance of probabilities, the panel concludes that the claimant was intending to travel to Canada on XXXXXX, 2008, and not to Cuba, as alleged; he invented his story of being persecuted by XXXXX for the purpose of submitting a refugee protection claim one month after he arrived in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimant intended to travel to Canada, not Cuba, and invented persecution story to submit refugee claim after arrival.

propositions.text: State is presumed capable of protecting citizens except in complete state breakdown situations.
propositions.quote: It should be assumed that the state is capable of protecting its citizens, except in situations of complete breakdown of the state apparatus.

propositions.text: International protection applies only if claimant has no alternative to state protection.
propositions.quote: The presumption that a state is capable of protecting its citizens reinforces the principle that international protection comes into play only if the claimant has no alternative.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the presumption that states can protect citizens except in total breakdown, so international protection applies only if no alternative exists.

propositions.text: Claimant must prove on balance of probabilities that state protection is inadequate.
propositions.quote: A claimant who alleges that state protection is inadequate must satisfy the Board that, on a balance of probabilities, the evidence establishes that state protection is inadequate.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant must prove state protection is inadequate on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he did not file complaint due to XXXXX's influence in Mexico.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that he had not filed a complaint with the Mexican authorities because it was not worth it, given XXXXX influence in Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant's assertion of XXXXX's influence is insufficient to justify not seeking protection or trying all options.
propositions.quote: the claimant's assertion that XXXXX had too much influence in Mexico is insufficient not to try to make use of all possible courses of action to obtain protection or to find out whether his country's authorities were able or willing to protect him.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports claimant's testimony; the court finds claimant's claim of XXXXX's influence insufficient to avoid seeking protection.

propositions.text: Even if XXXXX was influential, his influence was limited to XXXXXXXX state; claimant could seek protection in XXXXXX city far away.
propositions.quote: Even if the panel believed that XXXXX was an influential politician, the fact remains that his influence would have been limited to the state of XXXXXXXX, because he lived in XXXXX. It seems reasonable to believe that the claimant could have sought protection in XXXXXX, in the state of XXXXX, a city more than 1,700 kilometres from XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds XXXXX's influence limited geographically and claimant could have sought protection elsewhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: Panel rejects claimant's explanation as insufficient to explain why he did not seek protection before leaving.
propositions.quote: The panel rejects the claimant's explanation, finding it insufficient to explain why the claimant concluded that the authorities would not act on his complaint before he left his country.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to exhaust all possible courses of action before seeking international protection.
propositions.quote: In doing so, the claimant failed to exhaust all possible courses of action in his country before seeking international protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects claimant's explanation and finds he failed to exhaust all protection options before leaving Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant must show he took all reasonable steps to seek state protection and demonstrate interaction with authorities.
propositions.quote: The claimant must demonstrate that he has taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek state protection, given the context of the country in general. The claimant must also demonstrate the steps taken and his interaction with the authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant must prove he took all reasonable steps and interacted with authorities to seek protection.

propositions.text: Claimant is Mexican; Mexico functions normally and is presumed capable of protecting citizens.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a national of Mexico, a country that, according to the documentation, functions normally and is not in a situation of complete breakdown.

propositions.text: Claimant must seek state protection before claiming refugee protection in Canada.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the claimant's country is presumed to be capable of protecting him, and this requires him to seek this protection before claiming refugee protection elsewhere, in this case, here in Canada.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Mexico is making efforts to protect citizens and enable complaints by various means.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence shows that Mexico is making an effort to protect its citizens, by putting structures in place and adopting measures to enable citizens to file complaints. They can file a complaint by telephone, in person or online via the Internet.

propositions.text: No evidence shows claimant made serious effort or exhausted all courses to obtain state protection.
propositions.quote: In this case, there is nothing in the written or oral evidence demonstrating that the claimant made a serious and sufficient effort to obtain state protection or that he exhausted all courses of action open to him.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Mexico functions normally and claimant did not seriously try or exhaust state protection options before seeking refuge in Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant did not make serious effort or exhaust all courses of action to obtain state protection.
propositions.quote: Having concluded that the claimant did not make a serious and sufficient effort to obtain state protection and that the claimant did not exhaust all courses of action open to him in his country,

propositions.text: Claimant failed to rebut presumption that Mexico can protect him.
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the claimant was unable to discharge his burden of rebutting the presumption of protection that the state of Mexico would be able to offer him.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant failed to make sufficient effort and failed to rebut presumption Mexico can protect him.

propositions.text: To rebut presumption, claimant must provide clear and convincing evidence of state's inability to protect.
propositions.quote: To rebut the presumption of state protection, the claimant must provide "clear and convincing" evidence of the state's inability to protect (absent an admission by the national's state of its inability to protect that national).

propositions.text: Evidence must be reliable, probative, and satisfy balance of probabilities that protection is inadequate.
propositions.quote: The evidence that state protection is inadequate must not only be reliable and have probative value, but must also satisfy the Board that, on a balance of probabilities, state protection is inadequate.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant must provide clear, convincing, reliable evidence proving state protection is inadequate on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Claimant did not provide clear and convincing evidence that Mexico cannot or will not protect him.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the panel concludes that the claimant did not provide "clear and convincing" evidence that the Mexican state cannot or will not protect him.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant failed to provide clear and convincing evidence that Mexico cannot or will not protect him.

propositions.text: Claimant stated he faced discrimination for being homosexual: mistreatment at school, family abuse, job instability.
propositions.quote: In his narrative, the claimant stated that, because of his sexual orientation, he faced discrimination in his environment for years. At school, the teachers showed no sympathy, and his peers mistreated him. He alleged that he had to change schools three times and that his parents beat him and threw him out of the house when they discovered that he was homosexual. He also alleged that he was dismissed several times over the years and that it was very difficult for him to find a stable job.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports claimant's narrative of discrimination and abuse due to his homosexuality.

propositions.text: Panel accepts claimant is homosexual but finds discrimination allegations exaggerated to embellish claim.
propositions.quote: Although the panel accepts that the claimant is homosexual, it finds that the allegations of discrimination against him were exaggerated to embellish his claim, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts claimant's homosexuality but finds his discrimination claims exaggerated to embellish his case.

propositions.text: Claimant's amendments to PIF about schools and jobs contradict earlier statements showing normal school career.
propositions.quote: On August 15, 2011, the claimant submitted amendments to his Personal Information Form (PIF) to point out that he had attended six schools over the years and that he had worked in seven different locations between XXXXX 2003 and XXX 2005. However, at question 6 of his PIF, the claimant mentioned that he has 12 years of education, after attending one elementary school, one secondary school and one college. The panel sees nothing extraordinary about his school career.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's amendments contradict earlier statements and show a normal school career.

propositions.text: Claimant provided same info in Schedule 1 as initial PIF; claimed he did not pay attention to amendments.
propositions.quote: The information provided by the claimant at page 5 of the document Schedule 1, "Background Information," submitted as A-1, Immigration File, is the same information that he provided in his initial PIF. When asked why he had not provided the same personal information that he provided in the amendments when he submitted his refugee protection claim, the claimant answered that he had not paid attention.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for not providing amended info is unsatisfactory for reasons explained later.
propositions.quote: This explanation does not satisfy the panel, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant gave same info in Schedule 1 as initial PIF and finds his explanation for ignoring amendments unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Claimant declared info was complete and true; panel finds last-minute amendments were to harmonize narrative with homosexuality claim.
propositions.quote: When the claimant provided the information requested in this form, he declared that the information he gave was complete, true and correct. The panel notes that it is unreasonable for the claimant to wait until the day before his hearing to amend information as basic as his education and his list of employers. The panel concludes that the amendments were made at the last minute to harmonize the allegations in his narrative with respect to his homosexuality.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's last-minute amendments were unreasonable and made to align with his homosexuality allegations.

propositions.text: Claimant answered 'XXXXXXXXX' when asked who he feared if returned; no mention of discrimination or persecution based on homosexuality.
propositions.quote: Finally, in the same document, when asked, "Who are you afraid of if you were to return to your country?" the claimant answered "XXXXXXXXX" There is no mention of discrimination or of persecution based on his homosexuality.

propositions.text: Claimant gave no satisfactory reason for not mentioning sexual orientation fear.
propositions.quote: The claimant did not have a satisfactory reason when he was asked to explain why he did not mention his sexual orientation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant did not mention fear based on sexual orientation and gave no satisfactory explanation for omission.

propositions.text: Panel concludes alleged discrimination does not amount to persecution.
propositions.quote: In any event, the panel concludes that the discrimination alleged by the claimant does not amount to persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant's alleged discrimination does not constitute persecution.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant has an internal flight alternative in Mexico.
propositions.quote: Alternatively, the panel is of the opinion that the claimant has an internal flight alternative in Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant has an internal flight alternative within Mexico.

propositions.text: At hearing, claimant was asked about fears if living elsewhere in Mexico, e.g., La Paz or Mexico City.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the claimant was asked what he might fear if he returned and lived elsewhere in Mexico, such as in the city of La Paz, a Mexican city on the Gulf of California coast and the capital of Baja California Sur, or in Mexico City in the Federal District.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports claimant was asked about fears if living elsewhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant testified that XXXXX could find him anywhere in Mexico.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that XXXXX would be able to find him anywhere in Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports claimant testified XXXXX could find him anywhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: The claimant submitted no reason why it would be unreasonable to seek refuge in other cities within the meaning of case law.
propositions.quote: the claimant submitted no reason why it would be unreasonable, within the meaning of the case law,11 to go to one of these cities to seek refuge

propositions.text: The claimant submitted no real and concrete evidence of risk of persecution or cruel treatment.
propositions.quote: He also submitted no real and concrete evidence establishing the existence of conditions making it possible that he could run the risk of being persecuted on a Convention ground or face a risk to his life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant gave no reason or evidence showing it would be unreasonable to seek refuge elsewhere or that he faces persecution risk.

propositions.text: The burden of proof for internal flight alternative rests on the claimant.
propositions.quote: The burden of proof regarding an internal flight alternative rests on the claimant

propositions.text: Applicant must establish unreasonableness of seeking refuge elsewhere or conditions preventing relocation.
propositions.quote: the applicant had to establish either that it would be unreasonable for him to seek refuge in another part of the country or that there were, in fact, conditions preventing him from relocating elsewhere

paragraphs.summary: Justice Lagacé stated claimant bears burden to prove unreasonableness or impossibility of internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Burden of proof on internal flight alternatives is on the applicant.
propositions.quote: It is settled law that in matters concerning internal flight alternatives the burden of proof is on the applicant

propositions.text: Refugee claimant must show it would be unreasonable to seek refuge elsewhere.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the refugee claimant must demonstrate that it would be unreasonable for him or her to seek refuge in a different part of the country

paragraphs.summary: Justice Shore confirmed settled law that applicant must prove unreasonableness of internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Claimant must show on balance of probabilities a serious risk of persecution in areas with internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: the onus is on the claimant to demonstrate why, on a balance of probabilities, he faces a serious risk of persecution in a part of the country where there might be an internal flight alternative

paragraphs.summary: Court of Appeal held claimant must prove serious risk of persecution in areas with internal flight alternative on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: The claimant is a 26-year-old man with 12 years education and 5 years labor experience in Mexico.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a 26-year-old man with 12 years of education and 5 years of labour market experience in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant's age, education, and labor experience in Mexico.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the incidents occurred in 2008 or that the claimant is still of interest to XXXXX.
propositions.quote: the panel does not believe that XXXXX still has any interest in the claimant, given the passage of time

paragraphs.summary: The panel disbelieves the alleged 2008 incidents and that XXXXX still targets the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant did not discharge his burden of proof and has an internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: the claimant did not discharge his burden of proof, as set out in the case law,15 and concludes that he has an internal flight alternative

propositions.text: Internal flight alternative alone is sufficient to dispose of refugee claim under section 96 or subsection 97(1) IRPA.
propositions.quote: ...is in itself sufficient to dispose of the refugee claim," as stated by the Honourable Justice Shore in Palacios,16 above, under either section 96 or subsection 97(1) of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed burden and has internal flight alternative, which suffices to reject claim under IRPA.

propositions.text: The claimant cannot succeed as his fear has no objective basis and he can avail state protection.
propositions.quote: I determine that the claimant, XXXXXXXXXXXXXX, cannot succeed. The claimant's fear has no objective basis...because he can avail himself of state protection

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant's fear lacks objective basis and he can access state protection, so he cannot succeed.

propositions.text: The refugee protection claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: Consequently, his refugee protection claim is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The court orders rejection of the claimant's refugee protection claim.
